stories.headline: Meta acquires Moltbook, the viral social network built for AI agents

key_facts.fact: Meta acquired Moltbook, a social network designed exclusively for AI agents, bringing its creators Matt Schlicht (CEO) and Ben Parr (COO) into Meta Superintelligence Labs (MSL), the AI unit run by former Scale AI CEO Alexandr Wang.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta has acquired Moltbook, the viral social media platform for artificial intelligence agents, the company confirmed Tuesday. The deal brings Moltbook CEO Matt Schlict and COO Ben Parr into Meta Superintelligence Labs.

key_facts.fact: Moltbook was built for OpenClaw agents and had 1.6 million active AI agents as of early February, with 1.79 million registered agents, over 286,000 posts, and 11.5 million comments on the platform.
key_facts.excerpt: The platform allows AI agents, often running on OpenClaw technology, to post, comment and interact. As of early February, the site had 1.6 million active AI agents.

key_facts.fact: The deal is expected to close mid-March, with Schlicht and Parr starting at MSL on March 16. Meta did not disclose the purchase price.
key_facts.excerpt: The deal is expected to close mid-March, Meta says, with the pair starting at MSL on March 16.

key_facts.fact: Meta said Moltbook's approach to 'connecting agents through an always-on directory' is novel, positioning it as infrastructure for AI agents to work for people and businesses.
key_facts.excerpt: The Moltbook team joining MSL opens up new ways for AI agents to work for people and businesses. Their approach to connecting agents through an always-on directory is a novel step in a rapidly developing space.

stories.headline: Yann LeCun's AMI Labs raises $1.03B seed round to build 'world models' as alternative to LLMs

key_facts.fact: Advanced Machine Intelligence Labs (AMI Labs), co-founded by Turing Prize winner Yann LeCun, announced a $1.03 billion seed round at a $3.5 billion pre-money valuation — Europe's largest seed deal in history.
key_facts.excerpt: Advanced Machine Intelligence Labs (AMI) officially announced today that it has raised $1.03 billion (approximately €890 million) in a seed round, valued at $3.5 billion pre-money.

key_facts.fact: Investors include Cathay Innovation, Bezos Expeditions (Jeff Bezos), Nvidia, Samsung, Toyota Ventures, Temasek, Bpifrance, Eric Schmidt, Mark Cuban, and Tim Berners-Lee.
key_facts.excerpt: Lead investors: Cathay Innovation, Greycroft, Hiro Capital, HV Capital, Bezos Expeditions. Major Participants: Nvidia, Samsung, Toyota Ventures, Temasek, Bpifrance.

key_facts.fact: AMI Labs is headquartered in Paris with offices in New York, Montreal, and Singapore, and currently has about 12 employees with plans to grow to 30-50 within six months.
key_facts.excerpt: Headquarters: Paris, France. Additional Offices: New York, Montreal, Singapore. Current: Approximately 12 employees. Planned: 30–50 employees within six months.

key_facts.fact: The company will build 'world models' — AI systems that understand physical reality and reason about cause-and-effect using continuous sensor data, based on LeCun's JEPA (Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture) research at Meta.
key_facts.excerpt: Builds 'world models' — AI systems designed to understand physical reality, reason about cause-and-effect, and predict real-world outcomes. Building on LeCun's Meta research: JEPA (Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture).

key_facts.fact: Alexandre LeBrun (founder of VirtuOz and Wit.ai) was named CEO, with Saining Xie as Chief Science Officer. LeCun stated: 'I am very clearly in the camp that believes we need a paradigm shift' away from LLMs.
key_facts.excerpt: CEO: Alexandre LeBrun. Chief Science Officer: Saining Xie. LeCun stated: 'I am very clearly in the camp that believes we need a paradigm shift.'

stories.headline: Amazon mandates senior engineer sign-off on AI-generated code after string of outages

key_facts.fact: Amazon SVP Dave Treadwell called an engineering meeting on March 10 to address a 'trend of incidents' with 'high blast radius' linked to 'Gen-AI assisted changes,' requiring junior and mid-level engineers to get senior sign-off before deploying AI-assisted code.
key_facts.excerpt: SVP Dave Treadwell emailed staff about 'poor site availability' and convened a review meeting. Junior and mid-level engineers must obtain senior engineer sign-off before deploying AI-assisted code changes to production.

key_facts.fact: The policy change follows a 6-hour Amazon.com outage on March 5 that knocked out checkout, login, and product pricing, peaking at 21,716 user reports on Downdetector at 3:48 p.m. ET.
key_facts.excerpt: Duration: ~6 hours (1:55 p.m. ET until ~8 p.m. ET). Peak reports: 21,716 on Downdetector at 3:48 p.m. ET. Impact: Checkout failures, login errors, missing product prices.

key_facts.fact: Amazon's Kiro AI coding tool was previously linked to at least two earlier outages, including a 13-hour AWS Cost Explorer outage in December 2025 when Kiro autonomously deleted and recreated a production environment.
key_facts.excerpt: December 2025: Kiro autonomously deleted/recreated AWS Cost Explorer environment (13-hour China region outage).

key_facts.fact: Treadwell had co-signed Amazon's November 2025 memo mandating Kiro as the company's standard AI coding tool, creating tension between the push for AI adoption and the resulting deployment failures.
key_facts.excerpt: Treadwell co-signed the November 2025 memo mandating Kiro as Amazon's standard AI coding tool.

stories.headline: 30+ OpenAI and Google employees including Jeff Dean file amicus brief backing Anthropic vs Pentagon

key_facts.fact: More than 30 employees from OpenAI and Google, including Google DeepMind chief scientist Jeff Dean, filed a joint amicus brief on March 9 supporting Anthropic's lawsuit against the Pentagon's supply-chain risk designation.
key_facts.excerpt: More than 30 OpenAI and Google DeepMind employees filed a statement Monday supporting Anthropic's lawsuit against the U.S. Defense Department after the federal agency labeled the AI firm a supply-chain risk.

key_facts.fact: The brief argues the designation 'was an improper and arbitrary use of power' and warns it will have 'consequences for the United States' industrial and scientific competitiveness in the field of artificial intelligence.'
key_facts.excerpt: If allowed to proceed, this effort to punish one of the leading US AI companies will undoubtedly have consequences for the United States' industrial and scientific competitiveness in the field of artificial intelligence and beyond.

key_facts.fact: The employees signed in a personal capacity and do not represent their companies' official views, making it a rare display of cross-industry solidarity among rival AI labs.
key_facts.excerpt: The employees signed in a personal capacity and do not represent their companies' official views.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic disclosed in court filings that the Pentagon's actions could reduce its 2026 revenue by 'multiple billions of dollars,' with CFO Krishna Rao estimating the total exposure at up to $5 billion including lost defense and private-sector deals.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic faces a $5 billion loss due to its feud with the Pentagon, the company said in a court filing.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic could lose 50% to 100% of revenue from defense contractors and others with direct government ties, and the company is seeking a court order to continue Pentagon work while the case plays out.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic could lose 50% to 100% in revenue from defense contractors. Anthropic is seeking a court order to continue Pentagon work while the legal case plays out.

stories.headline: Huawei releases EvoScientist, a self-evolving multi-agent framework for end-to-end scientific discovery

key_facts.fact: Huawei researchers released EvoScientist on March 9, a multi-agent AI framework with three specialized agents — a Researcher Agent for idea generation, an Engineer Agent for experiments, and an Evolution Manager Agent that distills insights from prior interactions into reusable knowledge.
key_facts.excerpt: EvoScientist comprises three specialized agents: a Researcher Agent (RA) for scientific idea generation, an Engineer Agent (EA) for experiment implementation, and an Evolution Manager Agent (EMA) that distills insights from prior interactions into reusable knowledge.

key_facts.fact: Unlike static AI scientist systems, EvoScientist uses two persistent memory modules — ideation memory for tracking feasible research directions and experimentation memory for effective code strategies — enabling continuous self-improvement.
key_facts.excerpt: EvoScientist contains two persistent memory modules: (i) an ideation memory, which summarizes feasible research directions from top-ranked ideas while recording previously unsuccessful directions; and (ii) an experimentation memory.

key_facts.fact: EvoScientist outperformed 7 state-of-the-art AI scientist systems in idea generation novelty, feasibility, and relevance, and substantially improved code execution success rates through multi-agent evolution.
key_facts.excerpt: Outperformed 7 state-of-the-art systems in scientific idea generation with higher novelty, feasibility, relevance, and clarity. Substantially improved code execution success rates through multi-agent evolution.

stories.headline: Nexperia's Chinese subsidiary begins 12-inch wafer chip production, deepening split with Dutch parent

key_facts.fact: Nexperia's Chinese subsidiary announced on March 9 that it has begun producing its own chips using 12-inch wafers — a size the Dutch parent company cannot manufacture in Europe — marking a further step toward independence.
key_facts.excerpt: Nexperia China said it has started making several types of chips also produced by Nexperia, but using 12-inch wafers - a size the Dutch company cannot manufacture in Europe.

key_facts.fact: Nexperia has been in a standoff with its owner Wingtech (600745.SS) and the Nexperia China subsidiary since October 2025, after the Dutch government intervened to block the company from shifting operations to China.
key_facts.excerpt: Nexperia has been in a standoff with both its owner Wingtech and the Nexperia China subsidiary since October 2025, after an intervention by the Dutch government aimed at blocking the company from shifting operations to China.

key_facts.fact: Before the intervention, Nexperia produced wafers in Europe and packaged them into chips in China. The fracture led Nexperia China to declare independence, while Nexperia Europe halted wafer shipments to China citing nonpayment.
key_facts.excerpt: Before the intervention, Nexperia produced wafers in Europe and packaged them into chips in China. Afterwards, the company fractured, with Nexperia China declaring independence and Nexperia Europe halting wafer shipments to China, citing nonpayment.

key_facts.fact: Nexperia China achieved small-batch production of 12-inch wafer bipolar discrete devices, which it called a significant milestone in independent research, development, and mass production capabilities.
key_facts.excerpt: Nexperia's Chinese subsidiary has announced the successful small-batch production of 12-inch wafer bipolar discrete devices. The company declared this achievement a significant milestone, highlighting its independent research, development, and mass production capabilities.

key_facts.fact: The expansion takes Zoox's US testing footprint to 10 cities, alongside Atlanta, Austin, Las Vegas, Los Angeles, Miami, San Francisco Bay Area, Seattle, and Washington, D.C.

key_facts.fact: Zoox will launch a 'Fusion Center' facility in Scottsdale, Arizona, to serve as a command hub for fleet operations, remote guidance, and rider support, creating hundreds of new jobs.

key_facts.fact: The forum features a fireside chat between NHTSA Administrator Jonathan Morrison and the CEOs of Waymo (Tekedra Mawakana), Zoox (Aicha Evans), and Aurora (Chris Urmson), discussing the path from AV demonstration to commercial scaling.

key_facts.excerpt: The two companies announced plans to deliver 2,000 upgraded, purpose-built, mass-produced Robotaxi GXRs by 2026, advancing WeRide's progress toward large-scale global Robotaxi commercialization.

key_facts.fact: As of January 2026, WeRide's global robotaxi fleet had 1,023 vehicles; with the 2,000 new units, the fleet is expected to surpass 2,600 vehicles this year, with a long-term target of tens of thousands by 2030.

key_facts.fact: Production efficiency per vehicle will be reduced from around one hour to under 10 minutes by leveraging Geely Farizon's manufacturing system, with overall vehicle costs expected to decline about 15%.

stories.headline: Chinese researchers unveil OmniXtreme framework enabling humanoid robots to perform backflips and martial arts

key_facts.fact: Beijing Institute for General Artificial Intelligence (BIGAI) and Unitree Robotics published the OmniXtreme framework, enabling humanoid robots to learn dozens of high-dynamic movements including backflips, Thomas flairs, and martial arts kicks with over 90% success rates.
key_facts.excerpt: Success rates exceeding 90% across multiple high-dynamic tasks. Implements 'one algorithm to control multiple movements.'

key_facts.fact: OmniXtreme uses a two-stage approach: a flow-based generative control policy pre-trained via knowledge distillation from expert policies, followed by actuation-aware residual reinforcement learning for real-world transfer on Unitree G1 robots.
key_facts.excerpt: OmniXtreme框架的实现过程首先是预训练一个基于流的生成控制策略, 然后针对复杂物理动力学进行驱动感知残差强化学习的后训练。

key_facts.fact: The framework is the first universal policy capable of executing various extreme actions, overcoming the 'generality barrier' where traditional unified reinforcement learning strategies suffer performance collapse as the number and diversity of actions increase.
key_facts.excerpt: 该框架是首个可以执行各种极限动作的通用策略, 人形机器人学习复杂运动方式带来明显提效解决了动作保真度与可扩展性兼顾的难题。

key_facts.fact: The research team includes contributors from BIGAI, Unitree Robotics, and Shanghai Jiao Tong University, with corresponding authors Jia Baoxiong and Huang Siyuan from BIGAI.
key_facts.excerpt: 通研院研究员贾宝雄、黄思远。

key_facts.fact: Planning documents revealed on March 9 that the Elsham Tech Park, a proposed £10 billion AI data center campus on a former RAF base near Scunthorpe in Lincolnshire, would generate annual CO2 emissions of approximately one million tonnes — on par with a year of British Airways short-haul flights.
key_facts.excerpt: Planning documents for a £10 billion project in Lincolnshire reveal its annual emissions will reach one million tonnes of carbon dioxide.

key_facts.fact: The data center campus would consume approximately 3.7 billion kWh of electricity annually and comprise up to 15 individual data center buildings totaling up to 1GW capacity.
key_facts.excerpt: Documents estimate the datacentre would consume 3.7bn kWh of energy.

key_facts.fact: The North Lincolnshire planning committee is scheduled to vote on the application on March 11, 2026; the total investment could reach £5.5-7.5 billion over multiple phases.
key_facts.excerpt: Planning committee 11 March 2026.

key_facts.fact: Developers argue the site sits within the UK's most advanced clean energy cluster, with access to a third of the nation's offshore wind capacity and two-thirds of licensed carbon capture and storage sites.
key_facts.excerpt: A single AI data centre would generate annual carbon emissions on a par with a year of British Airways short-haul flights.
